# Theographic Bible Metadata

Theographic is a knowledge graph of the Bible, weaving data about people, places, and periods of time into the tapestry of God's story. This data enables smarter search algorithms, new apps, and exciting research potential. It's an open-source project to share information about the scriptures in our digital world.

...

## What's Inside

Every verse of the King James Version (1769) is linked to the people, places, events, and dictionary entries it mentions.

| Table | Records | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Books / Chapters / Verses | 66 / 1,189 / 31,102 | KJV text, authorship, and counts of people and places |
| People | 3,067 | Names, family relationships, groups, birth and death places and years |
| Places | 1,298 | Coordinates, feature types, gazetteer links, other names, part-of links |
| Events | 450 | Timeline with dates, durations, predecessors, participants, and locations |
| People groups | 23 | Tribes, apostles, and other groups |
| Easton's Bible Dictionary | 6,519 | Entries linked to people and places |

Chronology: The events timeline and people's birth and death years follow Dr. Floyd Nolen Jones, The Chronology of the Old Testament: A Return to the Basics. See Chronology and Dates.

## Getting the Data

| Folder | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `json/` | Preferred source. One file per table; link fields are arrays of record IDs. |
| `CSV/` | The same tables as CSV, plus `WordIndex.csv` (one row per KJV word). |
| `geo/` | GeoJSON for mapping: every place as a Linked Places gazetteer (`bible-places.geojson`) and Paul's journeys |
| `neo4j/` | Cypher scripts that build a Neo4j graph from the JSON |
| `api/` | A GraphQL API over the JSON, live at `https://theographic-api.netlify.app/api/graphql` |

## Documentation

# Download Bible Data

All of the information I have gathered to support this website and other projects is free to download from GitHub as part of the open-source Theographic project, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. It is structured to link every piece of information to related data. For example, a verse that mentions a person or place is tied to a record with details about that named entity. An entry in the events table links back to the verses that describe the event, the people involved, and the place where it happened. Below is an overview of what's in the database:

- Books, Chapters, and Verses: The text of the King James Version of the Bible (1769 edition), with all 31,102 verses linked to the writer and to the people, places, and events each verse describes.
- People and groups: Biographical details about 3,067 unique individuals, including alternate names, birth/death place and year (if known), family relationships, and the verses that mention the person by name. Individuals who can be identified with key groups such as a tribe of Israel, the disciples, or those in Jesus' genealogy are tagged as members of those groups.
- Places: 1,274 places with coordinates derived from openbible.info/geo, augmented with classification (region, city, water, etc.) and linkage to other databases of historical places such as Pleiades and GeoNames. Most locations are tagged with verse references, people who have been there, and events which occurred in that place.
- Events: A timeline of 450 events from Creation through Acts, with dates, duration, predecessors, participants, locations, and verses. Dates follow the chronology of Dr. Floyd Nolen Jones, The Chronology of the Old Testament, and dates in Acts follow timelines from Todd Atwood, ThM.
- Easton's Bible Dictionary: 6,519 dictionary entries linked to the people and places they describe.

## Formats

- JSON and CSV files for every table, plus a word-level index of the KJV.
- GraphQL API for querying the data live, with no download required.
- Neo4j import scripts that build a graph database you can explore with Cypher.
- GeoJSON for mapping, including the routes of Paul's journeys.
- Airtable for browsing and filtering the data in a spreadsheet-like view.

A field-by-field description of every table, along with the source bibliography and notes on how dates are numbered, is in the documentation. If you have questions or find an error, please open an issue on GitHub or email me (robert@viz.bible).

# Theographic Bible Metadata - Neo4j Graph Documentation

This documentation provides a reference for the structure, nodes, and relationships of the Neo4j graph database implementation of Theographic.

Neo4j is a graph database built for following connections through data, such as ancestry, social networks, and influence. Queries are written in Cypher, which describes a pattern of nodes and relationships to match. In Theographic, one query can find everything connected to a passage (people, places, events) or trace a person's complete ancestry.

...

**Requirements:**
- The **APOC** plugin (`apoc.load.json` and `apoc.periodic.iterate` are used by every import script).
- Outbound internet access from the database server. The scripts load JSON directly from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robertrouse/theographic-bible-metadata/master/json/`, so imports always use the latest published data on the `master` branch. To import a local or pinned copy, edit the URL at the top of each script.

...

### Node: `Verse`

| Property | Source field | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `id` | `id` | Airtable record ID |
| `osisRef` | `osisRef` | e.g. "Gen.1.1" |
| `verseId` | `verseID` | Sortable ID `BBCCCVVV`, e.g. "01001001" |
| `verseNum` | `verseNum` | Verse number (string) |
| `verseText` | `verseText` | KJV text |
| `mdText` | `mdText` | KJV text with Markdown links to people and places |

**Relationships:**
- `(:Chapter)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Verse)`
- `(:Verse)-[:MENTIONS]->(:Person)`
- `(:Verse)-[:MENTIONS]->(:Place)`
- `(:Verse)-[:DESCRIBES]->(:Event)`

...

### Node: `Person`

| Property | Source field | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `id` | `id` | Airtable record ID |
| `personId` | `personID` | Integer ID; also the suffix of the slug |
| `name` | `name` | Primary KJV name |
| `title` | `displayTitle` | Disambiguated title, e.g. "Joseph (son of Jacob)" |
| `alsoCalled` | `alsoCalled` | Alternate names |
| `gender` | `gender` | "Male" or "Female" |
| `description` | `dictionaryText` | Easton's Bible Dictionary text |
| `birthYear` | `birthYear` | String, ISO 8601 year (Jones) |
| `deathYear` | `deathYear` | String, ISO 8601 year (Jones) |
| `slug` | `slug` | e.g. "moses_2108" |
| `status` | `status` | Record validation status |

**Relationships:**
- `(:Person)-[:CHILD_OF]->(:Person)` and the reverse `(:Person)-[:PARENT_OF]->(:Person)`, from `mother`, `father`, and `children`
- `(:Person)-[:PARTNER_OF]->(:Person)`, created in both directions
- `(:Person)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(:PeopleGroup)`
- `(:Person)-[:BORN_IN]->(:Place)`
- `(:Person)-[:DIED_IN]->(:Place)`
- `(:Person)-[:PARTICIPATED_IN]->(:Event)`
- `(:Person)-[:WROTE]->(:Chapter)`
- `(:Verse)-[:MENTIONS]->(:Person)`

...

### 1. Ancestry & Family Trees
**Find the father and grandfather of King David:**
```cypher
MATCH (david:Person {name: "David"})-[:CHILD_OF]->(father)-[:CHILD_OF]->(grandfather)
RETURN father.name, grandfather.name

Connecting biblical knowledge to our world today

Theographic is a knowledge graph of the Bible, weaving data about people, places, and periods of time into the tapestry of God's story. This data enables smarter search algorithms, new apps, and exciting research potential. It's an open-source project to share information about the scriptures in our digital world.

## The data

3,067 people, 1,298 places, 450 events and23 groups, linked to 31,102 verses across 66 books and1,189 chapters. It is maintained in the open at theographic-bible-metadata.

Scripture text is the King James Version, 1769 edition, which is in the public domain. Dictionary entries are from Easton's Bible Dictionary (1897), also public domain.
